data.title: Fine-tuning
data.tagline: Continuing to train an existing model with task examples so its outputs better match them on a specific task
data.learningOutcome: You can tell what prompts, retrieved material, and fine-tuning each change, and know to evaluate with new examples.
data.description: A support team wants every refund reply to state the outcome before the next step. Fine-tuning can continue training a model with representative inputs and target replies; compare it on tickets not used for training to see whether it helps, and still provide the current task instructions.

learning.assumes: You have seen AI answer from a prompt but struggle to keep one kind of task consistent with team examples.
learning.outcome: You can tell what prompts, retrieved material, and fine-tuning each change, and know to evaluate with new examples.

distinctions.label: Prompt
distinctions.explanation: A prompt states the task and requirements for the current request; fine-tuning trains further on input and target-output examples. A fine-tuned model may still need prompts for the current goal and context.

distinctions.label: RAG
distinctions.explanation: RAG retrieves external material when answering; fine-tuning makes the model better match training examples. For changing refund policies, check current material rather than assuming a fine-tune updates itself.

explanation.title: Examples show the target behavior
explanation.text: Representative inputs and target outputs provide examples for further training. There is no single sample count that fits every model and task.

explanation.title: Evaluate on new inputs
explanation.text: Training examples do not prove that new requests will work. Keep tickets outside the training set and compare correctness, format, and tone.

data.boundary: It makes outputs better match training examples; it does not guarantee every new answer follows them or knows current policy. Use an updatable source for changing information.

lessonPractice.title: A team configured a support model. Which evidence shows this request actually used a fine-tuned model?

options.label: The model version in use has a training record based on paired support examples
options.feedback: This connects the model in use with further training on inputs and target replies: fine-tuning.

options.label: The current request adds reply-format requirements to its prompt
options.feedback: That can influence this answer, but changing a prompt does not show the model was trained further.

options.label: Retrieval found the updated return policy for this request
options.feedback: That supplies current source material through retrieval, not evidence of further model training.

data.agentPrompt: Do not start training yet. First use real support tickets and target replies to improve the prompt, then check tone and format on a separate set of tickets. If it is still inconsistent, explain what data fine-tuning would use, how you would evaluate it, and what it cannot guarantee.
